title: Depression years unloading rail cars and playing picnics
summary: During the Depression Glass worked for himself unloading gondola and gravel cars for little pay and played music when asked.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Who were you with? In the Depression? Yeah.

I was playing for myself in the Depression. I was working for myself. I'd get out there and work and unload cold cars. I'd catch a job playing, go to the lake or something like that, you know? And I'd play them picnics. You still unload them cold cars? I'd unload gondola cars by myself. I unload two a day by myself. One at night and one in the day. I'd unload it for George Kelly. I'd wheel it out. I was only making $10 a car. $10? That's all I made. Them big gondolas. Them big gondolas. I'd unload one in the day and one at night. I'd go to the union building and throw one over for Mr. Dillman. I'd throw one over the fence, slack, you know? Throw a car slack out by myself. And I'd wheel a car cold over with a big wheelbar.
Enough of the work you do now.
And you'd play music at night?
I'd play music. I'd be calm, I'd play music. If I didn't have nothing to do, I'd go play music. If anybody would come for me.
That man carry a heart right now.

Yeah, I've been working hard all my day. Hard work don't kill you. I've been working hard all my day. I'd get in the gravel car and throw one out by myself. And I can tell you this was the time I could unload one. I'd get in the gravel car for six o'clock, and four thirty of that evening, I'd throw that gravel car out by myself.
I'm glad it's you, not me.
Ain't going to miss you, look at the clock, when I get in there. And for four thirty I'd be and throw that car gravel out.
